source_refs.note: Topic 11.2.3 (Nomenclature of cycloalkanes) with Figure 11.3, printed page 249.

blocks.text: Cycloalkanes are named by attaching the prefix cyclo- to the name of the alkane with the same number of carbon atoms. Figure 11.3 shows ethylcyclohexane; isopropylcyclohexane (IUPAC 1-methylethylcyclohexane); n-propylcyclohexane (IUPAC propylcyclohexane); and 1,1,4-trimethylcyclohexane.

blocks.alt: Skeletal formulas of four substituted cyclohexanes: ethylcyclohexane (a two-carbon chain on the ring), isopropylcyclohexane, IUPAC (1-methylethyl)cyclohexane (a branched three-carbon group), propylcyclohexane (a straight three-carbon chain) and 1,1,4-trimethylcyclohexane (two methyls on carbon 1 and one on carbon 4, numbered on the ring).
blocks.caption: Naming cycloalkanes (original diagram after Figure 11.3).
